profile.description: Spot is HIGH/elevated with a long view down onto lower ground: a summit, ridge, bluff, rim, or scenic overlook. Recurs as the single dominant spatial signature; back-matter is explicit that the place is high.
From the spot one sees a broad, sweeping, open vista ('nature's wide embrace'): a wide panorama outward over valleys/water, not an enclosed view.
Cache is tucked in a natural above-ground rock recess: a crevice, niche, gap, undercut, or overhang at/against stone - reach in behind/under a rock, not buried.
Not buried, no digging: the box rests on or against an existing natural feature at or above ground level (ledge, shelf, hollow, base of tree/boulder).
The operative landmark is rock/stone - a boulder, slab, outcrop, ledge, or sittable rock at the spot ('a rock you can sit on'). Stone is the host feature.
Water is adjacent/visible but never crossed: a creek, river, pond, lake, or spring beside or below the spot. Spot stays on the dry bank/shore side.
Setting is woods/forest with an open clearing, meadow, or field edge nearby; the spot sits where forest meets open ground (often just past a tree line).
Reached on an established footpath/trail, just off it - not bushwhacking; near a road, an easy walk, non-dangerous footing.
Hard accessibility bound: within ~3 miles of a road, reachable on foot in under ~2 hours, no water crossing or cliff scaling.
Spot is hidden/secluded, slightly off the obvious view - around a bend, on the far/back or side of a feature, tucked just out of straight-line sight, rarely visited.
A gap/saddle/notch between two rock features (twin crags, paired outcrops, a cinched landform) frames the spot or its view.
A prominent tree as a natural marker at/near the spot - oak (shade) and pine recur; cache may sit at the base of a tree.
Spot/view oriented EAST (sunrise, eastern shore, notch facing east); the clearest single cardinal cue, though some cues point NE/other.
A distinctively rounded/domed/egg-shaped/circular stone as the marker (dome boulder, round disc, egg-rock). Most common shape echo, though competing with angular cues.
Green moss/lichen/vegetation against darker exposed stone as a color marker at the spot.
Hard, durable, crystalline/quartz-bearing or sparkling/gritty rock as the host material (corundum, rock crystal, quartz, mica glint).
Sharp, angular, faceted, six-sided or stepped/layered (stratified) rock rather than smooth - bedding lines, columnar/hexagonal, blocky rampart form.
Warm-toned color cue: reddish/iron-stained rock or red clay, or golden/sunlit stone; a lone red feature to align on.
Pale, white, clear/frosted, chalky, or quartz-white stone as the marker - light rock standing against darker surroundings.
A bowl-, cup-, or basin-like concave depression, hollow, or pit in the rock/ground at the spot (chalice, kettle, amphitheater cove).
Near a confluence or bend where two waters meet or a watercourse curves; spot sits at/above the junction or inside the bend.
Approach involves a descent ('go down') or a final curl/turn just before the high spot - down a slope into a draw, or the spot just past where the path bends.
A small, easily-overlooked inscription/mark/seam confirms the exact spot up close (read it, do not decode); look on undersides/bases.
Faint repeated 'left'/turn-left directional nudge at a decision point on the approach.
Spot is exposed to wind/rain (a breezy ridge/overhang) rather than a sealed cave - sheltered enough to protect the box but open to weather.
Possible short measured pace/number count from a fixed marker to the exact spot (numeric motifs flagged, no confident value).
